question: What have courts decided about who gets a Fed account?
answer: So far the courts side with the Fed. Two appeals courts (the Tenth Circuit for Custodia in 2025 and the Second Circuit for Banco San Juan in 2026) held that being eligible for a Fed account does not entitle a bank to one. Custodia has asked the Supreme Court to take the case, and the Fed opposed review on October 13, 2026.

items.title: Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62
items.text: Does statutory eligibility give a state-chartered bank a right to a Reserve Bank master account?
kv: Tenth Circuit (2025-10-31): eligibility for a master account is not an entitlement. Custodia petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-07-10 (No. 26-62); the Fed opposed review on 2026-10-13. The Court has not yet decided whether to hear it.

THE gate case. Every crypto bank, fintech trust, and state money experiment needs the Fed's rails; whether access is a right or a favor is now before the Court — or settled for a generation if cert is denied.

items.title: Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY & Board — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 25-1144
items.text: May a Reserve Bank terminate an existing master account under contract and risk process?
kv: Affirmed 2026-05-13: no statutory right to continued service; FRBNY's termination authority stands.
The gate swings both ways — an account once granted can be taken. Second and Tenth Circuits now converge on Reserve Bank discretion.

items.title: Fourth Corner Credit Union v. FRB Kansas City — D. Colo.; 10th Cir. 16-1016 (2017)
items.text: Must a Reserve Bank serve a state-chartered cannabis credit union?
kv: Fractured 1-1-1 judgment; amended lawful-purpose complaint allowed; no entitlement established. Later Custodia law rejects the entitlement reading.
The first crack at the gate question — three judges, three theories, no rule — showing why Custodia's published holding matters.

items.title: TNB USA v. FRBNY — S.D.N.Y. 1:18-cv-07978 (2020)
items.text: Did FRBNY unlawfully stall a "narrow bank" built to pass interest-on-reserves to depositors?
kv: Dismissed as unripe (2020) — no final denial, no merits ruling.
The narrow-bank idea — 100%-reserve money without lending — died in the waiting room, not in court. The gate can win by never answering.

rows.what: Tenth Circuit fractured Fourth Corner decision
rows.detail: Dismissal reversed in part; amendment allowed. Conditional lawful account theory may proceed. Time/place per the map: Docket time not stated; Byron White Courthouse, Denver, CO.

Master-account delay becomes judicial controversy. No immediate account access. Time/place per the map: Filing timestamp/locus not publicly stated; D. Wyo. electronic filing; Casper division is legal venue.

rows.what: BSJI complaint and PI motion (Banco San Juan)
rows.detail: Immediate account-termination challenge opens. Existing account temporarily subject to court request, not court protection. Time/place per the map: Filing timestamp not stated; S.D.N.Y. electronic filing; New York, NY operating Bank.

rows.what: BSJI preliminary injunction denied (Banco San Juan)
rows.detail: FRBNY may proceed under contracts/risk process. Account termination not judicially stopped. Time/place per the map: Signing/docket time not stated; Manhattan courthouse.
Judgment for Board and FRBKC. Denial remains operative. Time/place per the map: Time not stated; Ewing T. Kerr Courthouse, Casper, WY.
District judgment affirmed. Fed gate discretion confirmed. Time/place per the map: Docket entry date verified; release time not stated; Denver, CO.

rows.what: Second Circuit affirms in BSJI (Banco San Juan)
rows.detail: Judgment for FRBNY/Board. Account termination discretion confirmed. Time/place per the map: Release time not stated; Thurgood Marshall Courthouse, New York, NY.
Deadline moves to 2026-07-11. No change to Fed account denial. Time/place per the map: Order time not stated; Supreme Court, Washington, DC.

One day before the extended deadline, Custodia filed its petition for certiorari: whether the Fed may deny a state-chartered bank's master account without meaningful review. The Court docketed it July 14 as No. 26-62; a response is due August 13 absent waiver or extension. Docketing is not a cert grant, merits ruling, or master-account access.

Deadline met — the petition arrived 2026-07-10, one day early, and was docketed July 14 as No. 26-62. The next fixed clock is the August 13 response deadline absent waiver or extension; distribution and conference remain pending. Time/place per the map: Deadline time follows Supreme Court filing rules; Washington legal docket.
Amicus briefs supporting Supreme Court review were filed August 12-13 by the Blockchain Association, The Digital Chamber and Senator Lummis and others.

rows.what: The Fed opposes Supreme Court review (Custodia)
rows.detail: After two deadline extensions, the Board and the Kansas City Fed filed briefs asking the Court not to take Custodia's case.

uncertain: The Supreme Court has not decided whether to hear Custodia's case.

catalog_context.title: The court cases deciding who gets inside the money system
catalog_context.answer: A map of 72 case families and 159 dated events on who can hold a Fed account, which agencies survive and how far emergency money powers reach. So far the courts mostly leave gatekeeping power with the Fed, Treasury and bank receivers.

catalog_context.title: The Fed is many legal bodies, and its building cost doubled
catalog_context.answer: The Federal Reserve remains a congressionally created system of Board, FOMC and separately chartered Reserve Banks—not a literal fourth branch—but 2026 doctrine preserves exceptional cause protection for Governors.
